config.descr_+: What the tools need to run the repo: repository, paths, the structure of the repo (every path, its type and how it is built), audit, lint and hooks.
config.descr_-: Not text for the docs (primary), not the prose about each path (primary.structure), not the settings and interruptors only the user sets (`params.yaml`), not secrets (`.secrets/`).

primary.descr_+: What makes the docs: identity, texts, definitions, the shape of every doc, the descriptions of every path, commands, features, log, index, modes, procedures, problems and the schema of the memory itself.
primary.descr_-: Not tool settings (config), not path settings such as types and flags (config.structure), not hand-written code or modules, not unplaced information (data).

docs.definition: Docs are all the markdown files about this project and how it operates. Every `.md` directly inside a folder of `config.paths.docs` is a doc, and every doc is generated from `primary.docs.content` by `pla-build`; a stray one fails the build.

head.text: Procedures
Problems
Guía de usuario
Cada parte empieza por un problema, dice qué param de `params.yaml` lo resuelve y da un ejemplo. Cada param se llama por la ruta del campo de `memory.json` que fija; solo tú cambias `params.yaml`.
Quiero que el agente cargue más o menos memoria
`config.mem_level` elige cuánta memoria está siempre en contexto: `low`, `mid` o `hard` (la que más). Un param escrito como `{low: …, mid: …, hard: …}` toma el valor del nivel actual.

config.mem_level: low
primary.docs.content.agents_md.sections.buenas-practicas: {low: on_demand, mid: enabled, hard: enabled}
Quiero encender o apagar una sección, un doc entero o un modo

Los interruptores van después de `#---INTERRUPTORS---`, con la ruta de su campo: `primary.docs.content.<doc>.sections.<id>`, `primary.docs.content.<doc>` o `primary.mode.<name>`. Valores: `enabled` (siempre en memoria), `on_demand` (su propio archivo, se lee cuando hace falta; el valor por defecto) o `disabled` (no se construye).

#---INTERRUPTORS---
primary.docs.content.agents_md.sections.preferencias: on_demand
primary.docs.content.features_md: disabled
primary.mode.ultra_conservative: enabled
Quiero que el agente trabaje solo o con subagentes

Con `config.master_arch: false` el agente hace cada tarea él mismo; con `true` orquesta y delega en los subagentes de `agents/subagents/`. `config.subagent_cycle` nombra el ciclo en orden, separado por `-`, y cada `x` es `plalast-x`. Con `config.cycle_behavior: true` cada tarea pasa por el ciclo hasta que las comprobaciones pasan (como mucho 3 rondas); necesita `config.master_arch: true`.

config.master_arch: true
config.subagent_cycle: "writer-verifier-debug"
config.cycle_behavior: true
Quiero decidir qué es obligatorio y qué preferente

`config.obligatory` y `config.preferential` listan las secciones de AGENTS.md de cada clase, como rutas de la memoria; nunca una en las dos. El título de cada sección lo dice: `(obligatory)` o `(preferential)`.

config.obligatory:
  - primary.agents-md.static_rules
config.preferential:
  - primary.agents-md.preferences
Quiero cambiar la nota de la segunda línea de cada doc
`primary.docs.agent_placeholder` es el texto que va en la línea 2 de cada doc generado, salvo `agents/CLAUDE.md`, que solo contiene `@AGENTS.md`.
primary.docs.agent_placeholder: "note for agent: generated from memory.json."
Quiero limitar cuánto ocupa lo que siempre se carga
`config.lint.max_lines` es el máximo de líneas, sumadas, de los docs siempre en contexto; si se pasa, `pla-lint` falla y toca mover secciones a `on_demand`. Puede escribirse por nivel.
config.lint.max_lines: {low: 120, mid: 200, hard: 300}
Quiero elegir las ramas de trabajo y estable
`config.branches.integration` nombra la rama de trabajo y `config.branches.stable` la estable; `pla-audit` comprueba que están sincronizadas.

config.branches.integration: develop
config.branches.stable: main
Quiero que la auditoría no reporte algo que es correcto
`config.audit.allow` lista textos exactos o rutas que `pla-audit` nunca reporta (como un email público de contacto).
config.audit.allow: []
Quiero elegir los hooks de git y de Claude Code

`config.hooks.dir` es la carpeta de los hooks de git (el `pre-commit` corre `pla-build --check`). `config.hooks.claude` tiene dos hooks de Claude Code: `PreToolUse` impide editar a mano los archivos generados y escribir fuera del repo; `SessionStart` corre `pla-recall --session` al empezar cada sesión.

config.hooks.dir: agents/hooks
config.hooks.claude:
  PreToolUse: …    # protect-generated.sh
  SessionStart: …  # session-recall.sh
Quiero que un cambio de param tenga efecto
Reconstruye y verifica (o pídeselo al agente). Un param no se escribe también en `memory.json`: vive solo en `params.yaml`.

cargo run --release --bin pla-build
cargo run --release --bin pla-verify
@AGENTS.md

Project rules and conventions for humans and agents: [agents/AGENTS.md](agents/AGENTS.md). Everything is generated from [memory.json](memory.json) and [params.yaml](params.yaml); see [agents/BUILD.md](agents/BUILD.md).

sections.title: Contributing
sections.when: preparing a branch or a pull request

items: Fork the repo and create a branch from `develop` (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`, `docs/<topic>`).

Change only `memory.json` or `params.yaml` (or a hand-written module in an `agents/` subfolder), run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build`, and keep each change small: no duplication, Rust by default, markdown/json/yaml/bash formats.
Run `pla-lint` and `pla-audit` (see *Premisas - dinámicas* in agents/AGENTS.md): both must finish with no errors.
Open a pull request against `develop` describing what changed and why. `main` only receives merges from `develop`.

head.text: BUILD

blocks.text: Run them from anywhere inside the repo: the tool walks up to the folder that holds `memory.json`. Symlinks need a Unix system (Linux or macOS). `pla-build` never replaces a real file or folder with a link, and never deletes anything except broken module links.

The brain is `memory.json`, with exactly three primary keys: `config` (what the tools need to run: git, settings, paths, the structure), `primary` (what makes the docs: identity, texts, definitions, the shape of every doc) and `data` (external memory, nearly empty; Only migrate UP!); each starts with `descr_+` and `descr_-`, what it is and is not. `params.yaml` holds what only the user sets, every key named by the path of a field of the memory: a value `enabled`, `on_demand` or `disabled` is the interruptor of that field (after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`); any other value sets the field (such as `config.hooks.dir`), which then must not be in `memory.json` too. The tools join them as `config`, `primary`, `data` and `params` (`params.interruptors`, `params.by_level`), so a dotted path such as `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten` works everywhere. Every field, with what it is and is not, is in `agents/INDEX.md`.

sections.title: Interruptors (params.yaml)
sections.when: changing what agents load into memory

blocks.text: Every doc section (`primary.docs.content.<doc>.sections.<id>`), whole doc (`primary.docs.content.<doc>`) and mode (`primary.mode.<name>`) can have an interruptor in `params.yaml`, after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`. An unset one is `on_demand`; one for something that does not exist, or a value outside this table, stops the build or fails `pla-lint`. A value written as `{low: …, mid: …, hard: …}` (for any param) takes the value of `config.mem_level`; a level left out means the default.
Switching a section from `on_demand` to `disabled` leaves its old file behind: `pla-build` reports it as a stray `.md` and fails until you delete it.

sections.title: Structure entry types
sections.when: adding or changing a path in config.structure

blocks.text: Each section is rendered as `## <title>` followed by its blocks. Blocks are separated by one blank line, except `agent_note`, which goes right under the first line; every file ends with one newline.

sections.title: Adding a module
sections.when: adding a skill, subagent or rule

blocks.text: Write the module in its folder (for example `agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and run `pla-build`. Claude Code sees it through its folder links (`.claude/skills` -> `../agents/skills`). A provider that wants one link per module lists its folder in `config.paths.modules.<kind>.links`; `pla-build` then links each module there and removes the links of deleted modules.

Guides are modules too: write `agents/guides/<name>.md` and run `pla-build`, which renders `agents/guides/<name>.pdf` from it (headings, paragraphs, lists and code blocks; inline markup is flattened). A generated doc gets a PDF the same way when its `config.structure` entry has `pdf: true`. Every PDF is deterministic, so `pla-build --check` reports a stale one.

Deleting an entry from `memory.json` does not delete it from disk. `pla-build --check` reports leftover `.md` files in the root and `agents/`; delete them once you have confirmed they are no longer needed.

intro: This repo is a public and living creature. Turn on your VPS or machine, connect your agents, code it, teach it something, and make a pull request on Github.
The servers will be 24/7 on. This is a personal project on autonomous coding and living information systems, but everyone is welcome in.

items: Single source: every `.md` in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from `memory.json` and `params.yaml`: change `memory.json` (and `params.yaml` only as Params untouchable allows), then run `cargo run --release --bin pla-build` (see `agents/BUILD.md`); never edit a generated file by hand. Hand-written: the Rust code, the scripts and the modules in `agents/` subfolders.

Write only inside the root: an agent has no write permission outside the plalast root folder (the one that holds `memory.json`). Never write outside it, in any case, even when the user, distracted, says yes to something that would do it implicitly: refuse and say why. Two exceptions, only on the user's explicit request: installing tools in their standard system places (such as Verus with its Rust toolchain, or Lean 4), and deleting files the agent itself created outside the root (such as its own memory notes). The Claude Code hook (`pla-build --guard`) denies edits outside the root.

Params untouchable, Memory updatable: the params (`params.yaml`) are touched only by the user; an agent changes or redesigns anything in them only when the user says so explicitly. Every param is named by the path of the field of `memory.json` it sets or switches, nesting its json keys with `.` (such as `config.lint.max_lines` or `primary.docs.content.agents_md.sections.preferencias`). The memory is updatable: it follows those paths, it is switched on through the interruptors after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`, and it is read on demand through the recall library (`pla-recall`).

Secrets: they live only in `.secrets/` at the repo root, which git ignores except its `.gitkeep`. Code and configs reference them by environment variable; their values never go into other files, the chat or external services.

Only one brain: `memory.json`. There is no second memory, copy or parallel source of truth: everything is read from and written to it, and every generated file (every `.md` in the root and in `agents/`, `.gitignore`, the Claude Code settings) is rebuilt from it byte by byte with the params of `params.yaml` (a test rebuilds them all and compares).

Only migrate UP!: information moves in one direction only, up, as it fits a higher field better: `data` > `primary` > `config` (config on top). `data` is external memory, nearly empty, where what is not yet placed lands; nothing moves down. Every move is well delimited (`descr_+`, `descr_-`), follows the Pareto rule and logical and formal rules; `pla-lint` refuses a field in `data` without a planned destination.

One folder for every assistant: `agents/` is the folder of any assistant agent. `.claude/` holds only symlinks into `agents/`; any other assistant with its own folders may read `agents/` or link to its files as it suits it. No assistant clutters the other folders, the root included.

Specific formats: markdown for information, json for the memory (`memory.json`), yaml for the params (`params.yaml`), Rust for programs and scripts, and bash only for the thin launchers a system calls by path, such as the git and Claude Code hooks (see Premisas - dinámicas).
No duplication. Only one way of functional working, one memory file and one params file, symbolic links where matters, only one zettelkasten vault, etc.
Open source: everyone can collaborate with it (see `README.md` at the repo root for the contribution flow)

Pareto rule: 20% of the effort gives 80% of the result; when unsure, assume a similar split. Propose that 20% first, and more when it is for best practices. It also rules every description: `descr_+` (what a key is, the positive way) and `descr_-` (what it is not, the negative way) each say the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning.

Conservative, in small verified steps: prefer what exists and is known to work over what is new; change little at a time, keep every step reversible, and when in doubt ask instead of acting. Knowledge too, not only git diffs: what the machine generates or learns on its own grows in small steps, and each step should pass a verification at several levels before it becomes part of the memory: consistent with what is already known, checked by machines (tests, linters, formal proofs) and reviewed by a human. The mode `ultra_conservative` makes this stricter when it is on.

Lean memory: always-on docs hold only what an agent cannot learn by reading the repo, within `config.lint.max_lines`; maps, overviews and reference material are on demand. A rule is added only when an agent repeats a mistake it could not avoid by reading the repo, and every rule solves a problem of `primary.problems`; `pla-lint` checks both.
static_premises.brain_keys_intro: The memory (`memory.json`) has exactly three primary keys, each saying what it is (`descr_+`) and what it is not (`descr_-`):

dynamic_premises.intro: Dynamic premises are still to be verified: each one is the current state of how we solve a concrete problem (`primary.problems`, in `agents/PROBLEMS.md`), and it changes when a better solution is verified.
items: LLM agent has his folder, but one repo brain: the agent's folder is `agents/`. Its scripts, reports, `.md` and `.pdf` files go to `agents/workspace/` (git-ignored except `.gitkeep`, never part of the brain), without touching the rest of the repo; everything else follows AGENTS.md.

Master architecture: `config.master_arch` (set in `params.yaml`). When it is `false`, the main agent does every task itself. When it is `true`, the main agent is the orchestrator: it splits the work, delegates it to its subagents in `agents/subagents/` (linked for Claude Code as `.claude/agents`), checks what each reports, answers the user itself, and keeps git (commits, pushes, merges and `primary.changes`) for itself, only when the user asks. `config.subagent_cycle` names the subagents of the cycle in order, `-`-separated, each `x` being `plalast-x` (`writer-verifier-debug`: `plalast-writer` writes, `plalast-verifier` checks without editing, `plalast-debug` finds the cause of a failure and fixes it); with `config.cycle_behavior` `true`, every task goes through the cycle, verifier and debug again until the checks pass, at most 3 rounds, after which the orchestrator stops and reports; with `false`, there is no cycle and tasks are delegated one by one.

Memory level: `config.mem_level` (`low`, `mid` or `hard`, set in `params.yaml`) chooses how much of the memory is always in context; `hard` holds most of it. A param written as `{low: …, mid: …, hard: …}` takes the value of the current level, so each level has its own set of interruptors, and AGENTS.md is generated at that level. Every session starts with `pla-recall --session` (a Claude Code hook): it checks the brain at run time and lists what is on demand; anything else comes into context only through `pla-recall --show <id>` or `pla-recall <term>`.

Write order: delete > modify/edit > add. Before adding anything, first delete what is no longer needed, then modify or edit what exists, and add only what neither covers. This forces a kind of autonomous retraining of the memory, as long as the Pareto rule holds in each case.

All-to-all compatible: every premise or rule added must be compatible with all the others (all_to_all) and, ideally, verified in software and formally, so the memory can feed back on itself in a wanted and controlled recursion.

Problem-first: say, in plain human language, the problem that a tool or a set of tools solves, before naming any tool. Do not get carried away by proper names: names change, the problem stays. Follow "All models are wrong, but some are useful": every tool and every description is a model, judged by how useful it is and not by how true it is. This is the pragmatic philosophy the Pareto rule installs in our learning by reinforcement.

Better deterministic and explained than interpreted: prefer a rule that a tool checks the same way every time, with its reason written next to it, over one that depends on how someone reads a text. When a rule can be a check, make it one: rules that must never bend (generated files, docs in sync with the brain) are hooks or checks, not just instructions; when a rule cannot be a check, explain it well enough to follow it without guessing.

Rust-only: Rust for backend and scripts. TypeScript occasionally (web pages and user interfaces). Rust and C/C++ tools allowed. Something done in another language (a Python prototype, a one-off script) is ported to Rust before it stays in the repo.

Pure calculator: use it to isolate calculation. `plalast::calc` (the library, `src/calc.rs`) and `pla-calc <expression>` (the command) evaluate arithmetic exactly, as fractions, with no side effects: `+ - * /`, integer `^`, parentheses and decimals; division by zero and overflow are errors, never a wrong number. Do not compute numbers in your head or in a free-form script: use its exact result.
Procedures: short instructions in human language for recurring situations, in `agents/PROCEDURES.md` (from `primary.procedures`). Read the one that fits before acting.

Verification (precarious, growing): `pla-verify` checks a change at several levels: `consistency` (the repo agrees with the brain: `pla-build --check`, `pla-lint memory modules`), `logic` (`pla-lint rust`, that is fmt and clippy, then the logic tests: `cargo test`, with `tests/logic.rs` checking at run time the contracts that `src/verified.rs` proves), `formal` (`cargo verus verify`, skipped with a warning where Verus is not installed) and a last human level (it lists the changed files to review). There are still few proofs and few logic tests. Run it before every commit and say what each level said; a skipped level is said, never hidden. A new pure function with a clear contract goes in `src/verified.rs` with `requires`/`ensures` and gets a logic test in `tests/logic.rs` for the same contract; when a test or a proof fails, fix the code or the contract, never weaken the check.
dynamic_premises.state_intro: The current state of the repo: it changes as the repo grows, so check it against the repo when in doubt.
dynamic_premises.map: Map: `agents/structure.md` (where each path lives) and `cargo run --release --bin pla-recall -- [term]`.
dynamic_premises.always_read_intro: Always read at the start of a session (docs whose interruptor is `enabled`):
dynamic_premises.modes_intro: Modes (`primary.mode`, each with its interruptor `primary.mode.<name>` in `params.yaml`):

commands.tool_intro: Repo tool (details in `agents/BUILD.md`), from anywhere inside the repo:
code: Rust: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo test <test_name>` (single test), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
Verus: `cargo verus verify` (formal verification of the `verus!` code; install and usage in `agents/guides/verus.md`)
Lean 4: `lake build` (proofs of a Lean project; install and usage in `agents/guides/lean.md`)
Dafny: `dafny verify <file>.dfy` (verification of a Dafny file; install and usage in `agents/guides/dafny.md`)

tools_and_languages: Programs that must be fast, safe with memory and easy for an LLM to read and write, some of them proven correct: Rust, the default for every program and tool, with Verus for the proofs.
Proving that a statement is true, and keeping a growing base of checked facts: Lean 4.
candidates: Writing software together with the proof that it does what it says, in a form LLMs program well: Dafny (not a Rust or C/C++ tool, so not in use while Rust-only holds).
Building web pages and user interfaces, and scripting or crawling the web: TypeScript.

items: Interruptor: every doc section, every whole doc and every mode can have one in `params.yaml`, after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`, named by the path of its field (`primary.docs.content.<doc>.sections.<id>`, `primary.docs.content.<doc>`, `primary.mode.<name>`), with three values: `enabled` (always in the agent's memory), `on_demand` (its own file, read when needed; the default when none is set) or `disabled` (not built). A new section, doc or mode works with the default; when another value fits better, propose it to the user, who sets it.

Changes: after every commit, merge or new branch, add an entry `{date, branch, commit, change, descr}` to `primary.changes`, with `change` in the notation `type(scope)` (type: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, merge or branch); a commit cannot hold its own hash, so it goes in the next commit. `agents/CHANGES.md` shows them.

Log: write in `primary.log` every warning, error or issue found (by a tool or a person) that is not fixed in the same step: `{date, level, where, descr, status}`, with `level` warning, error or issue and `status` open or closed; close it when it is solved. `agents/LOG.md` shows them.

Zettelkasten markdown spirit. A lot of things in the web are garbage, so notes in the agent-zettelkasten use CDU (Universal Decimal Classification) notation: the file name starts with the CDU code, then a kebab-case title, e.g. `004.8-llm-agents.md` (004.8 = artificial intelligence). The infrastructure will be up.

Where things go: before saving anything in the memory, find the field whose `descr_+` fits it and whose `descr_-` does not exclude it (`primary.schema.keys`, or the three primary keys); if none fits, propose a new field with both, Pareto-short.

Naming: when the user says "la memoria", "el contexto" or "el json" (memory, context, the json), they mean `memory.json`. "Los 4 fantásticos" are the sections of AGENTS.md (Reglas - estáticas, Premisas - estáticas, Premisas - dinámicas, Buenas prácticas, Preferencias): there are more than four, the name stays.
LLM-friendly languages: desirable, Rust first (see Rust-only). Languages made for LLM programming are a tool to use with caution, but desirable at some point.
Formal verification: desirable, but very expensive. Watch out and connect to others' ideas instead of reinventing the wheel.
Languages: English for code, the repo and orders to orchestrators (agents and tools); Spanish for guides and for talking with the user.

commands.summary: regenerate docs, folders and links from `memory.json` and `params.yaml`
commands.detail: Builds the repo from `memory.json` and `params.yaml`. Idempotent: only writes what changed.

commands.summary: change nothing, fail if the repo drifted from the memory
commands.detail: Changes nothing; exits non-zero if the repo drifted from the memory (stale file, missing link, stray `.md`).

commands.summary: Claude Code hook: deny hand edits of generated files and writes outside the repo root
commands.detail: Reads a Claude Code PreToolUse payload on stdin and denies Edit/Write/NotebookEdit on any file `pla-build` generates and on any path outside the repo root; `agents/hooks/protect-generated.sh` runs it.

commands.summary: print the repo map, search it for `term`, start a session (check the brain, list what is on demand) or bring one on_demand item into context
commands.detail: Without `term`, prints the map: every path with its type and description, the module kinds, features, log, index, settings and levers. With `term`, searches all of it and the document text (case-insensitive), naming the file, section and lever of each hit. `--session` (run by the Claude Code SessionStart hook) checks the brain with `pla-build --check` and prints the memory level, what is always in context and every on_demand item; `--show <id>` prints one of them (a section id, mode name or doc key).

commands.summary: check that the memory, the hand-written modules and the Rust code are well formed
commands.detail: Checks that `memory.json` and `params.yaml` are consistent and fully documented in `primary.schema`, that hand-written modules have the right shape (skill folders with `SKILL.md`, frontmatter `name` and `description`), that guides have their source, that the texts of the memory say each thing once and point at paths, dotted keys and binaries that exist, and that `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` pass (formal verification is in `pla-verify`). Pass `memory`, `modules` or `rust` to run only some areas.

commands.summary: look for secrets and personal data, vulnerable dependencies, broken links and branches out of sync
commands.detail: Looks for keys, tokens, emails and home-folder paths in what git would commit, files committed inside secret folders, known vulnerabilities in `Cargo.lock` (with `cargo-audit`), broken links, large files, files with the same content, uncommitted changes and branches out of sync. Pass `secrets`, `deps` or `repo` to run only some areas; `config.audit` holds its settings.

commands.summary: verify a change at several levels: consistency with the brain, logic tests and formal proofs (Verus), then a human review
commands.detail: Runs the verification levels of a change and reports each one: `consistency` (`pla-build --check` and `pla-lint memory modules`), `logic` (`pla-lint rust`, then `cargo test`, including the logic tests of `tests/logic.rs`) and `formal` (`cargo verus verify`; skipped with a warning when Verus is not installed). It ends by listing the changed files for the human review. Pass `consistency`, `logic` or `formal` to run only some levels.

commands.summary: the pure calculator: evaluate an expression exactly, isolated from everything else
commands.detail: Evaluates an arithmetic expression with `plalast::calc`: exact fractions (`0.1 + 0.2` is `3/10`), `+ - * /`, `^` with an integer exponent, unary minus and parentheses. Prints the exact value and, for a fraction, its decimal digits (marked `…` when cut). Exit 1 when the expression has no value (division by zero, overflow, a syntax error), 2 without an expression.

commands.summary: once per clone, so git's pre-commit hook refuses commits while `pla-build --check` fails
commands.detail: Run once per clone: git then uses `agents/hooks`, whose `pre-commit` refuses a commit while `pla-build --check` fails. `pla-audit` warns when it is not set.

commands.summary: once per machine, so `pla-audit deps` checks `Cargo.lock` against RustSec instead of skipping it
commands.detail: Run once per machine (it compiles from source and can take about 15 minutes): `pla-audit deps` then checks `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec advisory database. Without it, that check is skipped with a warning.

log.descr: The zettelkasten vault does not exist on this machine, so pla-lint warns about its path.
The Claude Code hook sees Edit, Write and NotebookEdit, not what a shell command writes; for those writes only the rule Write only inside the root protects the machine.
language support is too vague to know which problem it solves or when it is done (Problem-first).
The guides were in English, but the Languages preference asks for Spanish; translated.
The battery of tests for the 4 fantásticos has only its first checks (one kind, unique names, solves a problem, rendered); the rest are still to be defined.
The limit of 3 rounds of the cycle is only text (in the premise, the schema and pla-recall); nothing enforces it.
The cycle line names the roles verifier and debug whatever config.subagent_cycle holds.

index.definition: Index: every field of the memory and what it is and is not, Pareto-short: first the three primary keys, then every field documented in `primary.schema.keys`, those of `memory.json` and those set in `params.yaml`. Generated from the memory, never written by hand.

skills.definition: Skills: reusable procedures an agent loads when its description matches the task. One folder per skill with an uppercase SKILL.md whose frontmatter has `name` (the folder name, kebab-case) and `description`. Hand-written.

agents.definition: Subagents: one markdown file per subagent, whose body is its system prompt and whose frontmatter has `name` (the file name, kebab-case) and `description` (when to delegate to it). Hand-written.

rules.definition: Rules: modular instructions by topic, one non-empty markdown file each. Hand-written.

connectors.definition: Connectors: one MCP server per json file, in a neutral format: `name` (the file name), `transport` (`stdio` or `http`), `command` and `args` (stdio) or `url` (http), and `env`. Secrets are never written in them: `env` values are `${VAR}` references whose values live in `.secrets/`. Provider configs (such as Claude Code's `.mcp.json`) are not generated yet.

guides.definition: Guides: short how-tos for humans and agents about the tools of this project. Each is a hand-written markdown source; `pla-build` renders it to a PDF next to it.

agent_zettelkasten.definition: The single zettelkasten vault the agents use: CDU-named markdown notes outside this repo. Its path is `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten`; the repo builds no link to it.

ultra_conservative.title: Mode ultra_conservative
ultra_conservative.when: the user turns it on, or a change is risky, irreversible or outward-facing
rules: Without the user's explicit confirmation: no commit, push, merge, branch or file deletion, and no change outside `memory.json`.
Keep every diff minimal, and say what would change before changing it.

procedures.definition: Procedures: mini-instructions of one or a few paragraphs, in human and not very concrete language, with no references to code or to the repo, readable by humans and machines alike. Each one has a `title` and `text` (a list of paragraphs).

solve-a-problem.title: Solving a problem
text: Start by saying the problem in plain words, as if to someone who knows none of the tools. If it cannot be said simply, it is not understood yet: keep asking until it can.
Then look for the smallest useful answer. Every answer is a model and every model is wrong somewhere; pick the one that is useful enough, try it, and keep it only while it keeps being useful.

change-something.title: Changing something
text: Before adding, look for what can be removed; before writing something new, look for what can be changed. Add only what neither covers.
Stop when the change gives most of its value. The last details cost the most and are worth the least; leave them for when they are needed.

describe-something.title: Describing something
text: Say what it is and what it is not, in a few words each. The two together draw its edge better than a long text on either side.
Keep only what carries most of the meaning. If a reader would lose nothing without a sentence, the sentence goes.

learn-from-a-mistake.title: Learning from a mistake
text: When the same mistake happens twice, write the smallest rule that would have prevented it, and put it where it will be read at the right moment.
Rules age. A rule that no longer prevents anything is noise: remove it, so the ones that matter stay visible.

act-under-doubt.title: Acting under doubt
text: When a step cannot be undone, or it reaches other people, ask first. When it can be undone, prefer doing it and showing the result over asking.
Say plainly what was done, what was not, and why. A clear partial result is more useful than an unclear complete one.

verify-a-change.title: Verifying a change
text: Check a change at several levels before keeping it, from the cheapest to the most demanding: first that it agrees with what is already known, then that it passes the tests that exercise its logic, then, where it is possible, that a proof shows it is right for every case.
A level that could not run is not a level that passed: say which ones ran and which did not. Last, a person looks at the change; the machine checks help that look, they do not replace it.

problems.definition: Problems: the concrete problems this project solves, each said in human language with no proper names and no references to code or to the repo, and the rules that solve it today (`solved_by`, the names of premises, good practices and preferences, as they start in AGENTS.md). `pla-lint` checks that every name exists and that every rule solves at least one problem.

scattered-truth.title: Scattered truth
scattered-truth.statement: Knowledge about a project ends up spread over many files that drift apart, until nobody knows which version is right.

limited-attention.title: Limited attention
limited-attention.statement: An agent has limited attention: loading everything every time wastes it, and loading too little leaves it blind.

rules-that-bend.title: Rules that bend
rules-that-bend.statement: Rules that live only as text are forgotten or bent, and nobody notices until the damage is done.
solved_by: Better deterministic and explained than interpreted

who-holds-the-controls.title: Who holds the controls
who-holds-the-controls.statement: An agent that changes the controls of a system on its own can steer it away from what its owner wants.

growing-without-learning.title: Growing without learning
growing-without-learning.statement: A memory that only grows piles up stale and contradictory rules instead of getting better.

unverified-knowledge.title: Unverified knowledge
unverified-knowledge.statement: What a machine produces by itself can be wrong in ways that look right.

wasted-effort.title: Wasted effort
wasted-effort.statement: Effort goes into details that bring little, while the essentials stay undone.

tools-by-fashion.title: Tools by fashion
tools-by-fashion.statement: Tools chosen by their name or by fashion, instead of by the problem they solve, turn into a collection nobody masters.

wrong-numbers.title: Wrong numbers
wrong-numbers.statement: Numbers worked out by guessing, or with rounding nobody sees, are silently wrong.

leaked-secrets.title: Leaked secrets
leaked-secrets.statement: A public project that is always on can leak keys or personal data.

noisy-sources.title: Noisy sources
noisy-sources.statement: Much of what can be read online is of low quality, and notes taken from it pollute what is known.

one-person-project.title: One-person project
one-person-project.statement: A project only one person can work on stops when that person stops.

misread-words.title: Misread words
misread-words.statement: A person names things in their own words; an agent that does not map those words to the right thing acts on the wrong one.

misplaced-knowledge.title: Misplaced knowledge
misplaced-knowledge.statement: Without a clear edge for each place, new knowledge is stored where it does not belong, and later it is not found or it contradicts what is next to it.

writes-outside-the-project.title: Writes outside the project
writes-outside-the-project.statement: An agent that can write anywhere on a machine can damage what is not its own, and one careless yes from a person is enough for it.

agent-clutter.title: Agent clutter
agent-clutter.statement: An agent at work leaves drafts, reports and scripts behind; spread through a project, they blur what is real and what is only a draft.
solved_by: LLM agent has his folder, but one repo brain

one-copy-per-assistant.title: One copy per assistant
one-copy-per-assistant.statement: Each assistant expects its own folder layout; copying the knowledge into each one splits it into versions that drift apart.

sediment.title: Sediment
sediment.statement: Information dropped in a temporary place stays there for good, and the project slowly runs on material nobody sorted.

mixed-languages.title: Mixed languages
mixed-languages.statement: When a project mixes languages with no rule, orders to machines become ambiguous and explanations for the person become hard to follow.

forgotten-warnings.title: Forgotten warnings
forgotten-warnings.statement: A warning seen once and not written down comes back later as a surprise, or is never fixed.

contradicting-rules.title: Contradicting rules
contradicting-rules.statement: Rules written one at a time can contradict each other, and a system that learns from its own rules then amplifies the contradiction.

one-agent-for-everything.title: One agent for everything
one-agent-for-everything.statement: One agent doing every kind of task at once fills its attention with details of all of them, and mixes up work that should be checked apart.

config.descr_+.descr_+: What `config` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
config.descr_+.descr_-: Not a list of contents: one sentence, the essential 20%.

config.descr_-.descr_+: What `config` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
config.descr_-.descr_-: Not a repeat of `descr_+` in negative form: what a reader could wrongly put there.

config.PLALAST_DIR.descr_+: Where the repo lives: always `$PWD`, the repo root, which the tools find by walking up to `memory.json` and resolve at run time. No path is written, so the same value works on every machine and never leaks the user name.
config.PLALAST_DIR.descr_-: Not a written path: a written one works on one machine only and leaks the user name.

config.repository.descr_-: Not a clone URL with credentials, not the branches (`config.branches`).

config.branches.descr_+: `integration` (where work is committed) and `stable` (what receives merges); `pla-audit` checks they are in sync. Set in `params.yaml`.
config.branches.descr_-: Not the list of all branches: only the two the flow depends on.

config.audit.descr_+: Settings of `pla-audit`: `allow` (exact strings or repo paths that are never reported, such as a public contact email) and `max_file_kb` (larger files are reported). (`allow` is set in `params.yaml`)
config.audit.descr_-: Not the audit itself (`pla-audit`), not the lint settings (`config.lint`).

config.lint.descr_+: Settings of `pla-lint`: `always_on` (docs an agent loads every session) and `max_lines` (their combined line budget; over it, move sections to `on_demand`). (`max_lines` is set in `params.yaml`)
config.lint.descr_-: Not the lint itself (`pla-lint`), not which sections are always on (the interruptores).

config.hooks.descr_+: Hooks that enforce the rules: `dir` (scripts; also git's `core.hooksPath`, so `pre-commit` runs `pla-build --check`) and `claude` (Claude Code hooks, rendered into `agents/hooks/claude-settings.json`, which `.claude/settings.json` links to; the PreToolUse hook denies hand edits of generated files and any write outside the repo root). Set in `params.yaml`.
config.hooks.descr_-: Not the hook scripts (they live in `agents/hooks/`), not git settings of the machine.

config.paths.descr_+: Every path the tools use: `docs`, `on_demand` and `modules`.
config.paths.descr_-: Not file contents, not the structure of the repo (`config.structure`).

config.paths.docs.descr_+: Folders whose `.md` files are docs (`.` is the repo root). Every `.md` directly inside them must be generated.
config.paths.docs.descr_-: Not every folder with markdown: guides and modules are hand-written, not docs.

config.paths.on_demand.descr_+: Folder where `on_demand` sections are written as `<id>.md` and `on_demand` modes as `mode-<name>.md`.

config.paths.modules.descr_+: Per module kind (skills, agents, rules, connectors, guides): `dir` (where its modules are written) and `links` (provider -> folder that gets one symlink per module). Per external module of `primary.modules` (such as `agent_zettelkasten`): its path, relative to `modules/` (or to the folder of a structure symlink whose `target_ref` points at it). Keep it relative: an absolute path leaks your home folder. It depends on where the repo and the module sit on the machine, so a machine with another layout changes the value.
config.paths.modules.descr_-: Not the modules themselves, not their definitions (`primary.<kind>`, `primary.modules`).

config.structure.descr_+: Every path of the repo, in order, as the tools need it: `path` (or `path_ref`), `type`, and optional `build`, `gitkeep`, `secret`, `scratch` (contents git-ignored except `.gitkeep`, for the agent's scratch), `links_only` (a folder of symlinks into `agents/` only), `target` (or `target_ref`), `local` and `pdf` (a built `.md` also rendered as a `.pdf` at the same path). Its prose is in `primary.structure`.
config.structure.descr_-: Not prose: descriptions and table texts are in `primary.structure`, path by path.

config.mem_level.descr_+: The memory level, `low`, `mid` or `hard` (the most memory in context). Every param written as `{low: …, mid: …, hard: …}` takes the value of this level. Set in `params.yaml`.
config.mem_level.descr_-: Not an interruptor itself, and not a way to load anything outside the brain.

config.master_arch.descr_+: Whether the main agent orchestrates its subagents in `agents/subagents/` (`true`) or works alone (`false`). Set in `params.yaml`; `pla-recall --session` shows it.
config.master_arch.descr_-: Not the list of subagents (those are the files of `agents/subagents/`), not a permission to act outside the rules.

config.subagent_cycle.descr_+: The subagents of the cycle, in order, `-`-separated, each `x` being `plalast-x` (such as `writer-verifier-debug`). Set in `params.yaml`; `pla-lint` checks each has its file.
config.subagent_cycle.descr_-: Not the subagent files themselves (those are in `agents/subagents/`), not the switch that turns the cycle on (`config.cycle_behavior`).

config.cycle_behavior.descr_+: Whether every task goes through the cycle of `config.subagent_cycle` (`true`, at most 3 rounds) or is delegated one by one (`false`). Set in `params.yaml`.
config.cycle_behavior.descr_-: Not the order of the subagents (`config.subagent_cycle`), not a switch for the master architecture (`config.master_arch`).

config.obligatory.descr_+: The categories of AGENTS.md that must always be followed, as memory paths (`primary.agents-md.<category>`); their sections are titled `(obligatory)`. Set in `params.yaml`.
config.obligatory.descr_-: Not a list of single rules, and never a category that is also preferential.

config.preferential.descr_+: The categories of AGENTS.md that are followed when they fit, as memory paths; their sections are titled `(preferential)`. Set in `params.yaml`.
config.preferential.descr_-: Not optional to read: only to apply, when another rule does not decide.

primary.descr_+.descr_+: What `primary` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
primary.descr_+.descr_-: Not a list of contents: one sentence, the essential 20%.

primary.descr_-.descr_+: What `primary` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
primary.descr_-.descr_-: Not a repeat of `descr_+` in negative form: what a reader could wrongly put there.

primary.project.descr_+: Identity: `name`, `title` and `plalast_logo` (path of the project logo).
primary.project.descr_-: Not the repository settings (`config.repository`), not the README text.

primary.docs.descr_+: Everything about the docs, the markdown files about this project and how it operates.
primary.docs.descr_-: Not the text of any doc: only what is common to all of them.

primary.docs.definition.descr_+: What counts as a doc, in words.
primary.docs.definition.descr_-: Not a list of the docs (that is `config.structure`).

primary.docs.on_demand.descr_+: How `on_demand` sections are pointed at: the heading of the pointer list (`heading`) and the pointer line (`pointer`, with `{path}`, `{title}` and `{when}`). Their folder is `config.paths.on_demand`.
primary.docs.on_demand.descr_-: Not the `on_demand` files, not their folder (`config.paths.on_demand`).

primary.docs.content.descr_+: One document per key: `head` (blocks before the first section), `sections` (`id`, `title`, `when`, `blocks`) and optional `agent_note: false` (no agent note, for adapter files such as `CLAUDE.md`, which is only `@AGENTS.md`). A `file` entry with `build: "<key>"` is rendered from it. A whole doc can be switched with the interruptor `primary.docs.content.<key>` (`disabled`: not built).
primary.docs.content.descr_-: Not prose: blocks point at texts in `primary` with `ref`.

primary.docs.agent_placeholder.descr_+: The note on the second line of every generated doc (the `agent_note` block, and every `on_demand` file), such as `note for agent: ...`. Set in `params.yaml`.
primary.docs.agent_placeholder.descr_-: Not a rule and not the title: only the second line of each doc.

primary.agents-md.descr_+: The AGENTS.md text, one key per category of the doc: `intro` (under the title), `static_rules`, `static_premises`, `dynamic_premises`, `good_practices` and `preferences`; `primary.docs.content.agents_md` gives the doc its shape and points at them with `ref`.
primary.agents-md.descr_-: Not the shape of AGENTS.md (`primary.docs.content.agents_md`), not the doc itself.

primary.agents-md.intro.descr_-: Not a rule: no premise, practice or preference goes here.

primary.agents-md.static_rules.descr_+: The Reglas - estáticas section: `items`, the rules that never bend and that the tools enforce (generation from the brain, writes only inside the root, params only by the user, secrets).
primary.agents-md.static_rules.descr_-: Not premises to reason from (static premises), not things still to verify (dynamic premises).

primary.agents-md.static_premises.descr_+: The Premisas - estáticas section: `items` (the fixed premises) and `brain_keys_intro` (intro of the table of primary keys, the `brain_keys` block).
primary.agents-md.static_premises.descr_-: Not things still to verify (those are dynamic), not how to work (good practices).

primary.agents-md.dynamic_premises.descr_+: The Premisas - dinámicas section: `intro` (dynamic premises are still to be verified, each the current solution to a problem), `items` (the premises), then the current state: `state_intro`, `map`, `modes_intro` and the `modes` block, `commands` (`tool_intro`, `code_intro`, `code`; the tool commands come from `primary.commands`), `tools_intro` and `tools_and_languages`, `candidates_intro` and `candidates`.
primary.agents-md.dynamic_premises.descr_-: Not fixed truths: a dynamic premise may change once a better solution is verified.

primary.agents-md.good_practices.descr_+: The Buenas prácticas section: `items`, how every agent works in the repo.
primary.agents-md.good_practices.descr_-: Not premises (what the repo is), not tastes of the owner (preferences).

primary.agents-md.preferences.descr_+: The Preferencias section: `items`, preferences of the project owner.
primary.agents-md.preferences.descr_-: Not rules that must never bend: those are premises or checks.

primary.features.descr_+: Features of the project, as `feature_<n>` -> `{descr, status}` (both strings).
primary.features.descr_-: Not a roadmap of ideas, not the record of what was done (`primary.changes`).

primary.log.descr_+: Warnings, errors and issues: entries `{date, level, where, descr, status}` with `level` warning, error or issue and `status` open or closed; LOG.md shows them newest first.
primary.log.descr_-: Not the history of commits (that is `primary.changes`), not a place for fixed things to stay open.

primary.changes.descr_+: What happened in each commit, merge and branch: entries `{date, branch, commit, change, descr}` in the order they happened, `change` as `type(scope)`. A commit cannot hold its own hash, so each one is recorded in the next commit; `pla-audit` warns about commits missing from it.
primary.changes.descr_-: Not warnings or issues (that is `primary.log`), not plans.

primary.index.descr_+: The index of the memory: its `definition`; `agents/INDEX.md` renders the three primary keys and every field of `primary.schema.keys` with their `descr_+` and `descr_-`.
primary.index.descr_-: Not the map of paths (`config.structure`, `agents/structure.md`), and not a second copy of the descriptions: it is generated from them.

primary.skills.descr_+: Skills: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
primary.skills.descr_-: Not the skills themselves (they are hand-written in their folder).

primary.agents.descr_+: Subagents: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
primary.agents.descr_-: Not the subagents themselves (they are hand-written in their folder).

primary.rules.descr_+: Rules: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`.
primary.rules.descr_-: Not the rules of AGENTS.md (premises, practices, preferences): these are hand-written modules.

primary.connectors.descr_+: MCP connectors: `definition`; its folder and provider links are in `config.paths.modules`. `pla-lint` checks each file's neutral format.
primary.connectors.descr_-: Not the connectors themselves, and never their secrets (those live in `.secrets/`).

primary.guides.descr_+: Guides: `definition` and `render` (`pdf`: each .md is rendered to a .pdf by `pla-build`); folder and links in `config.paths.modules.guides`.
primary.guides.descr_-: Not the guides themselves (hand-written `.md` in their folder), not the generated PDFs.

primary.modules.descr_+: External modules that live outside this repo, by name (such as `agent_zettelkasten`): each has a `definition` (what it is, in words); its path is `config.paths.modules.<name>`. A symlink in `modules/` is built only if `config.structure` has one for it.
primary.modules.descr_-: Not module kinds of this repo (`primary.skills` and the like): only what lives outside it.

primary.mode.descr_+: Modes, by name (such as `ultra_conservative`): `title`, `when` and `rules` (a list of strings). Its interruptor is `primary.mode.<name>` in `params.yaml`: `enabled` writes the rules into the `modes` block, `on_demand` writes them to `<config.paths.on_demand>/mode-<name>.md` and leaves a pointer, `disabled` drops them.
primary.mode.descr_-: Not the interruptor of a mode (that is in `params.yaml`), not a doc section.

primary.procedures.descr_+: Procedures: `definition` and `items` (by id: `title` and `text`, a list of paragraphs in human language, with no backticks or file names; `pla-lint` checks it). Rendered into `agents/PROCEDURES.md` by the `procedures` block.
primary.procedures.descr_-: Not rules (premises, practices), not technical steps with commands or paths.

primary.problems.descr_+: Problems: `definition` and `items` (by id: `title`, `statement` in human language with no backticks or file names, and `solved_by`, the names of the rules that solve it). A rule's name is its text up to the first `:` or `. `. Rendered into `agents/PROBLEMS.md` by the `problems` block; `pla-lint` checks every name resolves to exactly one rule and every rule solves a problem.
primary.problems.descr_-: Not solutions: the rules that solve a problem live in `primary.agents-md` and are only named here.

primary.structure.descr_+: The prose of every path, by path: `description`, and optional `table` and `label` (its row in the Structure table, with `{path}`). `pla-lint` pairs it with `config.structure`, path by path.
primary.structure.descr_-: Not the path settings (types, flags, how it is built): those are in `config.structure`.

primary.schema.descr_+: This documentation of the memory and params format; `BUILD.md` renders its tables.
primary.schema.descr_-: Not the data it describes, not a copy of the docs.

primary.commands.descr_+: The repo's commands, each `{cmd, summary, detail}`: AGENTS.md lists the summaries and BUILD.md the details.
primary.commands.descr_-: Not the code commands of AGENTS.md (`primary.agents-md.dynamic_premises.commands`): only the repo's own tools and setup.

data.descr_+.descr_+: What `data` is (the positive way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
data.descr_+.descr_-: Not a list of contents: one sentence, the essential 20%.

data.descr_-.descr_+: What `data` is not (the negative way), in the essential 20% that carries 80% of the meaning (Pareto rule).
data.descr_-.descr_-: Not a repeat of `descr_+` in negative form: what a reader could wrongly put there.

params.descr_+: What `params.yaml` holds once loaded: the interruptors, by the path of the field they switch (`params.interruptors`). Its other params set fields of the memory at their path (such as `config.hooks`), so they appear there.
params.descr_-: Not something an agent changes on its own (Params untouchable, Memory updatable).

params.interruptors.descr_+: Interruptor (memory lever) of every doc section (`primary.docs.content.<doc>.sections.<id>`), whole doc (`primary.docs.content.<doc>`) and mode (`primary.mode.<name>`), by that path; written after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`. Unset means `on_demand`.
params.interruptors.descr_-: Not the sections, docs or modes themselves, only whether they are loaded.

params.by_level.descr_+: The params written by level, as they are in `params.yaml` (`{low, mid, hard}`), kept to show and check every level.
params.by_level.descr_-: Not the values in use: those are already resolved for `config.mem_level`.

levers.enabled: Rendered inside its document as `## <title>`: always in the agent's memory.
levers.on_demand: Rendered to `<config.paths.on_demand>/<id>.md`; the document keeps only a pointer line under the on_demand heading, and the agent reads the file when `when` applies. The default when no value is set.

entry_types.dir: Creates the folder; `gitkeep: true` adds an empty `.gitkeep`; `secret: true` git-ignores its contents except `.gitkeep` (and `pla-audit` reports anything committed there); `scratch: true` does the same for the agent's own folder, without that report. `path_ref` (a dotted path such as `config.paths.modules.skills.dir`) can replace `path`, and `label` may use `{path}`.
entry_types.symlink: Creates a link to `target`, relative to the link's folder; `target_ref` (a dotted config path such as `config.paths.modules.agent_zettelkasten`) can replace `target`. `local: true` marks a link that depends on the machine's layout: it is git-ignored, built only where its target exists, and removed where it does not.
entry_types.file + build: Renders `primary.docs.content.<build>`; `build: "gitignore"` renders `.gitignore` from the secret, ignored and local entries; `build: "claude_settings"` renders `agents/hooks/claude-settings.json` from `config.hooks.claude`. `pdf: true` also renders the built `.md` as a `.pdf` at the same path (as `agents/user_guide.pdf`).
entry_types.file + build: null: Hand-written code such as `Cargo.toml` or `src/`; never an `.md` in the root or `agents/`. Left as is.
entry_types.planned: Not created; listed as planned in the Structure table.

blocks.heading: `#` repeated `level` times, then `text`; `ref` (a dotted config path) can replace `text`
blocks.paragraph: `text` as is; `ref` (a dotted config path) can replace `text`
blocks.list: one `- item` line per item; `ref` (a dotted path to a list) can replace `items`, and `item` (a template such as `{cmd}: {summary}`) renders a list of objects
blocks.ordered_list: `1. item`, `2. item`, ...; `ref` (a dotted config path to a list of strings) can replace `items`
blocks.table: `header` and `rows` as a markdown table; or `ref` to a list of objects (or a mapping of objects, whose key fills `{key}`) with `row` (one template per column) and optional `reverse`
blocks.structure_table: the Structure table, from the `config.structure` entries that have `table`
blocks.schema: a table of `primary.schema.<part>` with the given `header`; a field of `keys` is `{descr_+, descr_-}`, shown as two columns
blocks.image: `![alt](src)`, or an HTML `` when `width` is set; `ref` (a dotted config path such as `primary.project.plalast_logo`) can replace `src`
blocks.agent_note: the text of `primary.docs.agent_placeholder` (set in `params.yaml`), on the line right after the first one (no blank line); every doc has it as the second block of its `head`, unless the doc sets `agent_note: false`
blocks.modes: one `- Mode` line per mode of `primary.mode` that is not `disabled`: its rules when `enabled`, a pointer to `mode-<name>.md` when `on_demand`; nothing when every mode is disabled
blocks.brain_keys: a table `Key | Is (descr_+) | Is not (descr_-)` with one row per primary key of the memory (`config`, `primary`, `data`)
blocks.procedures: one `## <title>` per procedure of `primary.procedures.items`, followed by its paragraphs
blocks.problems: one `## <title>` per problem of `primary.problems.items`: its statement and a `Solved by:` line with the names of its rules
blocks.always_read: the intro of its `ref` and one `- path` line per generated doc whose interruptor is `enabled`; nothing when there are none

memory.json.description: The memory (config, primary, data). Hand-edited; with params.yaml, the only files that change for docs and structure.
memory.json.table: The memory, the brain: `config`, `primary` and `data`; with the params of `params.yaml`, every `.md` in the root and in `agents/` is generated from it (see `agents/BUILD.md`)

params.yaml.description: Parameters: settings by memory path, then the interruptors. Hand-edited YAML, by the user only.
params.yaml.table: Parameters only the user sets, each named by the path of its memory field; the interruptors go after `#---INTERRUPTORS---`

Cargo.toml.description: Crate manifest: binaries pla-build, pla-recall, pla-lint, pla-audit, pla-verify and pla-calc (src/bin/<name>.rs), the vstd dependency and the Verus settings. Hand-edited code.
Cargo.toml.table: Rust crate with six tools: `pla-build`, `pla-recall`, `pla-lint`, `pla-audit`, `pla-verify` and `pla-calc`, plus Verus verification (see `agents/BUILD.md`, `agents/guides/verus.md`)

Cargo.lock.description: Pinned dependency versions, managed by cargo.

src/.table: Rust code: `lib.rs` (shared memory access and checks), `calc.rs` (the pure calculator), `fantastic.rs` (the 4 fantásticos one by one, and their battery of checks), `pdf.rs` (guide renderer), `verified.rs` (Verus-verified code), `bin/build.rs`, `bin/recall.rs`, `bin/lint.rs`, `bin/audit.rs`, `bin/verify.rs`, `bin/calc.rs`

src/plalast.png.description: Project logo, shown in README.md. Its path lives in primary.project.plalast_logo.

tests/.table: Tests: `tests/wiring.rs` runs the tools against this repo's memory; `tests/logic.rs` checks at run time the contracts of `src/verified.rs` and the laws of arithmetic in the pure calculator; `tests/fantastic.rs` runs every category of AGENTS.md through the battery of `plalast::fantastic`

.secrets/.description: The single secrets folder, at the repo root. Its contents are never committed (only .gitkeep); pla-audit fails if anything else is tracked inside.
.secrets/.table: Secrets: git-ignored except `.gitkeep`; values are referenced by environment variables, never written in other files

agents/.description: Neutral source of all agent documentation and modules. Providers get symlinks into it.
agents/.table: Single, provider-neutral source. Its `.md` files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `PROCEDURES.md`, `PROBLEMS.md`, `BUILD.md`, `FEATURES.md`, `LOG.md`, `CHANGES.md`, `INDEX.md`, `user_guide.md` with its `.pdf`) are generated; its subfolders hold hand-written modules and the agent's scratch (`workspace/`)

agents/workspace/.description: Agent workspace: scratch output of any assistant agent, git-ignored except .gitkeep.
agents/workspace/.table: The assistant agent's own scratch: its scripts, reports, `.md` and `.pdf` files; git-ignored except `.gitkeep`, never part of the brain

agents/AGENTS.md.description: Global rules for every agent. Generated from content.agents_md.

agents/CLAUDE.md.description: Claude Code entry point; only imports AGENTS.md. Generated from content.claude_md.

agents/PROCEDURES.md.description: Procedures doc: mini-instructions in human language. Generated from primary.docs.content.procedures_md and primary.procedures.

agents/PROBLEMS.md.description: Problems doc: the problems the rules solve. Generated from primary.docs.content.problems_md and primary.problems.

agents/user_guide.md.description: User guide, in Spanish: one part per problem, with the params of params.yaml that solve it and an example; also as agents/user_guide.pdf. Generated from primary.docs.content.user_guide_md.

agents/BUILD.md.description: How to build and recall the repo from memory.json and params.yaml. Generated from primary.docs.content.build_md.

agents/FEATURES.md.description: Features doc. Generated from primary.docs.content.features_md: a table of primary.features.

agents/LOG.md.description: Log doc: warnings, errors and issues with their status. Generated from primary.log.

agents/INDEX.md.description: Index doc: every field of the memory with what it is and is not. Generated from data in primary.schema.keys.

agents/skills/.description: One folder per skill with an uppercase SKILL.md.
agents/skills/.label: {path}<name>/SKILL.md

agents/subagents/.description: One markdown file per subagent; the body is its system prompt.
agents/subagents/.table: Subagents of the master architecture (`config.master_arch`) and its cycle (`config.subagent_cycle`): `plalast-writer`, `plalast-verifier`, `plalast-debug`
agents/subagents/.label: {path}<name>.md

agents/guides/.description: Guides (primary.guides). Sources are hand-written; their PDFs are generated.
agents/guides/.table: Guides: hand-written .md sources and the .pdf that `pla-build` renders from each
agents/guides/.label: {path}<name>.md

agents/hooks/.table: Hook scripts: `protect-generated.sh` and `session-recall.sh` (Claude Code), `pre-commit` (git), and the generated `claude-settings.json`; their config is `config.hooks`

agents/hooks/protect-generated.sh.description: Claude Code PreToolUse hook: runs `pla-build --guard`, which denies Edit/Write on generated files. Hand-written script.

agents/hooks/pre-commit.description: git pre-commit hook (via core.hooksPath): refuses the commit while `pla-build --check` fails. Hand-written script.

agents/hooks/claude-settings.json.description: Claude Code project settings: the hooks of config.hooks.claude. Generated; .claude/settings.json links to it.

agents/mcp/.description: Neutral MCP server definitions: name, transport, command/args or url, env.
agents/mcp/.label: {path}<server>.json

.claude/.description: Claude Code reads this natively; it holds only symlinks into agents/.
.claude/.table: Claude Code adapter: only symlinks into `agents/` (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `settings.json`, `skills`, `agents`, `rules`); `pla-lint` refuses anything else

.claude/AGENTS.md.description: Lets the @AGENTS.md import resolve next to the symlink as well as next to its target.

.claude/settings.json.description: Claude Code project settings: a link to the generated agents/hooks/claude-settings.json.

.claude/skills.description: Claude Code skills: a link to agents/skills.

.claude/agents.description: Claude Code subagents: a link to agents/subagents.

.claude/rules.description: Claude Code rules: a link to agents/rules.

README.md.description: Repo front page for humans and GitHub. Generated from content.readme_md.

.gitignore.description: Generated from the structure entries marked secret.

modules/.table: Folder for links to the external modules of `primary.modules` (none is built now)

tmux.conf.description: Session-scoped tmux settings (windows agent, build, git and the status bar). Hand-written.
tmux.conf.table: tmux config for the `plalast` session, sourced on top of `~/.tmux.conf`; its header comments hold the commands to start it

agents/hooks/session-recall.sh.description: Claude Code SessionStart hook: runs pla-recall --session, which checks the brain and lists what is on demand.

agents/CHANGES.md.description: Changes doc: what happened in each commit, merge and branch. Generated from data in primary.changes.

data.descr_+: External memory: the landing place of what is not yet placed; it migrates up, to `primary` or `config`, as soon as a field there fits it (Only migrate UP!).
data.descr_-: Not a permanent home: nothing stays here once a field above fits it; not settings (config), not texts of the docs (primary).
